Emely M. Amoloza is a faculty member whose scholarly output and thesis supervision record in this repository span from 2022 to 2026. The available data indicates that they have advised six theses during this period, with the most recent supervision activity occurring in 2026. In addition to their supervisory role, they have authored two articles within this repository, with their latest item recorded in 2026. Their research interests appear to be interdisciplinary, bridging social sciences, business, media studies, and educational technology. The sub-topics associated with their items reveal a diverse range of academic engagement. Business and entrepreneurship is a prominent area, appearing in three of their items. This focus intersects with other fields such as social media, culture and identity, and agriculture and food. For instance, one thesis examines the influence of social media marketing on sneaker enthusiasts in Metro Manila, while another investigates how Korean TV dramas affect the purchase intentions of Korean food among college students in the Philippines. These studies suggest a keen interest in consumer behavior, market trends, and the economic implications of cultural phenomena.

Environment and sustainability, management and leadership, and arts and creative practice also feature in their portfolio. Two theses advised in 2026 highlight a strong connection between environmental policy and organizational behavior. One study, titled "Lingkod Bayang Makakalikasan," explores the determinants of employees' intention to engage in green behavior within a public organization, utilizing the theory of planned behavior. Another 2026 thesis, "Banning Single-Use Plastics and Compliance Intentions in a Public Market in Davao City," analyzes the psychological and social factors influencing vendors' compliance with plastic bans. These works demonstrate an ability to guide research that applies theoretical frameworks to practical, contemporary societal issues. The arts and creative practice topic is represented by a 2024 study on Filipino Generation Z’s perception of P-Pop’s potential as a global phenomenon. This research, which employed a quantitative-descriptive design, indicates an engagement with youth culture and media impact.

Journalism and news media, along with youth and family, are other areas of focus. A 2024 capstone project titled "Living in Two Worlds: A Documentary on Balancing Life with an Autistic Child" addresses the experiences of Filipino mothers parenting children with autism spectrum disorder. This multimedia study suggests that Amoloza supports research that combines journalistic techniques with sensitive social topics. Teacher training is another distinct area, evidenced by their own 2023 article evaluating the PLDT Infoteach Outreach Program. This study used thematic analysis to assess perceptions of digital skills among Filipino teachers and students, highlighting an interest in educational outreach and corporate social responsibility. Furthermore, their 2022 article on prototyping a blended physical education course for mixed volleyball points to an involvement in online and distance learning methodologies. This work investigates the feasibility of delivering team-based sports education in an open and distance e-learning environment. Overall, the fact sheet presents a profile of an adviser with a broad research scope, capable of supervising projects that range from consumer psychology and environmental sustainability to media studies and educational technology. The consistency of their output across these varied topics suggests a versatile approach to academic supervision, grounded in both quantitative and qualitative methodologies.
